title: Nonlinear electron-phonon interactions from first principles
abstract: Electron-phonon interactions underpin a variety of phenomena, ranging from transport and superconductivity to polarons and ultrafast carrier dynamics. Despite being one of the most intensely studied subjects in condensed matter physics, research on electron-phonon physics mostly focused on linear, first-order couplings. Second- and higher-order nonlinear couplings are commonly ignored because their calculations are too demanding and we lack computational frameworks that can provide both diagonal and off-diagonal coupling matrix elements. In this work, we report a theory and computational method for computing nonlinear electron-phonon interactions of any order in real materials. Our approach combines the advantages of unit-cell calculations of electron wavefunctions and supercell calculations of phonon perturbations, is systematically improvable, can be used with either semilocal or nonlocal exchange-correlation functionals, and is amenable to Wannier-Fourier interpolation. As a first proof of concept, we illustrate this method by computing second-order electron-phonon coupling matrix elements in diamond, lithium fluoride, and graphite as representative nonpolar semiconductors, polar semiconductors, and metals, respectively. Furthermore, we generalize the ab initio polaron equations to second-order electron-phonon couplings, and we show that second-order couplings are essential to achieve quantitative accuracy in polaron formation energies and hopping barriers. The present methodology will find application in the study of all properties and phenomena that are currently being investigated within the linear electron-phonon coupling approximation, from phonon-mediated superconductivity to excited-states dynamics, both in harmonic and anharmonic systems.
summary: This paper introduces a novel, systematic computational method to calculate nonlinear electron-phonon interactions of any order directly from first principles. By extending beyond linear approximations, the authors show that these higher-order couplings are crucial for accurately predicting key properties like polaron binding energies. This methodology promises to advance the study of charge transport and excited-state dynamics in various materials.
main_problem: The primary goal is to develop a first-principles theory and computational method to calculate nonlinear electron-phonon interactions of arbitrary order, overcoming the limitations of existing linear-coupling approximations.
main_result: The authors present a systematic framework to compute second-order (and higher) electron-phonon coupling matrix elements, demonstrating that these nonlinear terms are essential for achieving quantitative accuracy in polaron formation energies.
method: The method combines unit-cell calculations of electron wavefunctions with supercell calculations of phonon perturbations, allowing for the calculation of complex Born-von-Kármán integrals.
model_or_system: The physics centers on electron-phonon coupling, which governs phenomena like superconductivity, polaron formation, and carrier dynamics. The calculations are applied to representative materials including diamond, lithium fluoride, and graphite.
key_observables: Second-order electron-phonon coupling matrix elements ($g^{(2)}$), electron quasiparticle energy shifts (e.g., Debye-Waller correction), polaron formation energies, and hopping barriers.
important_parameters: The calculation is sensitive to the order of coupling (second-order being a key focus) and the nature of the exchange-correlation functional used (semilocal or nonlocal).
main_assumptions: The method is designed to overcome the limitations of the rigid-ion approximation (RIA) and the computational difficulty of calculating off-diagonal, nonlinear coupling terms.
figures_summary: Not specified in the notes, but the methodology involves mapping unit-cell wavevectors to the reciprocal space of the BvK supercell.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the physical necessity of nonlinear couplings, then details the novel computational framework combining unit-cell and supercell calculations to evaluate the required coupling integrals, and finally validates the method by computing $g^{(2)}$ for three distinct material classes.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter, the rigorous, systematic, and *ab initio* nature of developing a general computational framework for higher-order interactions is highly relevant to modeling complex, non-adiabatic dynamics in quantum systems.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Relation between the reciprocal space of the unit cell and that of the BvK supercell. This example illustrates a two-dimensional square lattice with lattice parameter a and BvK supercell of size 3×3 unit cells. The black dots are the reciprocal lattice vectors of the BvK supercell, G. The circles are the reciprocal lattice vectors of the unit cell, g. The filled gray square is the unit-cell Brillouin zone, and the blue dot is a representative k point inside the Brillouin zone. The other blue dots are the set of points k+g. For each such point, there is a unique G in the supercell reciprocal lattice. The circle denotes the wavevector cutoff (in this example, 5 × 2π/a).

FIG. 2. Workflow for calculating second-order electron- phonon coupling matrix elements via finite differences. The orange boxes indicate unit-cell DFT calculations, and the blue boxes indicate supercell DFT calculations. The Brillouin zone (BZ) grid for the unit-cell calculations equals the number of unit cells in the BvK supercell.
